snippet: Section 3.2: "Every recursive algorithm requires at least one base case that produces a direct result without generating further recursive subproblems. Without an explicit base case, call stack frames accumulate monotonically until a stack overflow exception halts the runtime."
relevance_reason: Direct formal definition of recursive base case requirement and stack overflow mechanisms.

snippet:
Slide 18: "Rules of Recursive Invariants:
1. Establish Base Case (simplest atomic input where answer is known)
2. Recurrence Step: Ensure arguments strictly converge towards base case
3. Activation Records: Every recursive invocation pushes a new stack frame containing local variables and return address."
relevance_reason: Step-by-step guideline and memory layout diagram for recursive functions.

snippet: Prof. Miller at 38:21: "Watch the debugger here: if you omit the `if (node == null) return;` guard in pre-order traversal, the instruction pointer will blindly dereference a null pointer or enter an infinite loop pushing frames until memory exhaustion. Always check your base case first!"
relevance_reason: Live lecture walkthrough debugging stack overflows and base case omissions.
